blurb: Landslides, mudflows and debris flows: soil mechanics, triggers, flow physics, runout, monitoring and risk.

pics.alt: Black-and-white photograph of the Vajont arch dam with the landslide mass filling the reservoir behind it, 1963
pics.caption: The Vajont dam, Italy, after the rockslide of 9 October 1963: about 270 million m³ of rock from Monte Toc filled the reservoir behind the dam. The arch dam survived, but the displaced water overtopped it and destroyed Longarone.
pics.title: Vajont Dam landslide.jpg

pics.alt: Aerial view from offshore of the coastal bluff above La Conchita, California, with houses, a railway and Highway 101 at its foot
pics.caption: La Conchita, California, seen from offshore in 2009. The bluff above the town failed in 1995, and in January 2005 part of that landslide remobilised (about 200,000 m³), killing 10 people.
pics.title: LaConchitaLandslide.jpg
